summary: Rabbi Besser discusses the lessons of Parashat Vayesse, focusing on how Yaakov Avinu handled his departure from Lavan and his marriage to two sisters. He explores the importance of patience and communication when inspiring family members toward religious growth, as well as the significance of keeping one's word even when not strictly obligated by law.
questions: How should one approach family members when trying to inspire them to become more religious?
Why did Yaakov Avinu marry two sisters if it was later prohibited by the Torah?
What is the significance of a person taking a personal commitment or Kabbalah upon themselves?
How does the Ramban explain the observance of mitzvot outside of Eretz Yisrael?
